habitat: Pairs when breeding, otherwise large flocks in woodland and bushveld. In Kruger it lives with people at rest camps during winter.
summary: A common resident. The head and breast are glossy blue, the wings glossy green and the eyes yellow. The identification line says the flanks and belly are purple, while the description says royal-blue. A blackish ear-patch and rows of black wing spots separate it from Cape Starling. The immature is duller, with sooty underparts and a grey eye. The call is sque-eear. The Kemp name Greater Blue-eared Starling and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Cape Starling lacks the dark ear-patch and has uniformly blue-green underparts and yellow eyes.

head.pattern: Head glossy blue, with a blackish ear-patch.

underparts.pattern: The identification line says the flanks and belly are purple. The description says the belly and flanks are royal-blue, and blue rather than magenta.

wings.pattern: Glossy green wings, with two variable rows of black spots on the coverts.

viewNotes.note: Glossy blue head and breast, green wings and a blackish ear-patch.
Yellow eyes. The belly is purple on the identification line and royal-blue in the description.
Rows of black spots on the wing coverts.
The underwing colour is not given.

calls.description: 'sque-eear, sque-eear-eeear'. No grade A recording from South Africa was found. The selected file is a grade A call from Zambia. The filename is XC584694-Greater Blue-eared starling (call) 20200722,BangweuluWetlands,ZAMBIA_2.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The belly is purple on the identification line and royal-blue in the description, so no belly colour is stored. Sooty is not a vocabulary colour. The grade A call is from Zambia. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^15=32768 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 16384–65536.
